newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil in top position to attract capital - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Brazil in top position to attract capital - Salomon.

text.p: Salomon Brothers Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Deryck Maughan said Brazil was one of the top five emerging markets to attract foreign investment and this trend was likely to continue in the next few years.
"Brazil has an unusual opportunity to succeed," he said. "It has a political maturity and an experience of capitalism and markets that distinguishes it from many other investment opportunities.
"The desire to invest in the United States and in Europe and in Japan in countries like Brazil is very strong. I believe that is structural, I think that is continuing," he said.

Maughan, who was on a three-day visit to Brazil to launch the Rio de Janeiro office of Banco Patrimonio, Salomon's 50/50 joint venture with local partners, said Brazil ranked second or third among emerging markets after China and possibly Russia in terms of foreign investment.

He said of the 12 countries to receive 70-75 percent of the $240 billion in total foreign capital supplied to emerging economies in 1996, five were predominant: China, Russia, Brazil, India and Indonesia.

Maughan said Brazil needed to implement the necessary structural reforms, currently on their way through Congress, and increase its company listings on the New York Stock Exchange in order to take full advantage of increasing capital flows in its direction.

"It is a disappointment that there are so few Brazilian companies listed in New York," he said. "I think it's important for Sao Paulo and for the economy at large that Brazil has full representation on the New York exchange, which is where American investors go first."

Banco Patrimonio Corporate Finance Director Luiz Chrysostomo said Brazil was expected to become the most attractive emerging market for foreign capital in the next three years given the country's impending privatizations in the electricity and telecommunications sectors.

Salomon's head of Latin American investment banking, Alberto Verme, said institutional investors in equities and in bonds, as well as strategic industrial investors had all increased their interest in Brazil in recent years.

Chrysostomo said Banco Patrimonio decided to open an office in Rio de Janeiro to consolidate the already strong presence Salomon Brothers had established there through a number of financial transactions involving Rio-based companies like Eletrobras, Petrobras and Aracruz Celulose.
Salomon Brothers was the first international investment bank to form a local partnership in Brazil and is now the first to open an office in Rio de Janeiro.

Sao Paulo-based Banco Patrimonio started off in 1993 with $80 million in managed assets, which has now risen to $1.6 billion, and has carried out 42 mergers, acquisitions and other corporate financial transactions in Brazil worth more than $5 billion.
